note: Design section, 72h window (cutoff ~2026-07-29T22:00Z). WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-run (shared across parallel librarians), so most collection was done via direct RSS/feed + og/JSON-LD date verification (curl) rather than search. The 72h design x AI hard-news pool was genuinely thin: SIGGRAPH 2026 (Jul 19-23) announcements, Adobe Firefly Assistant, Runway/Midjourney/Sora model news, Config 2026, Autodesk Neural CAD all fell outside the 72h window; VentureBeat and TheVerge were unfetchable (429 / blocked UA) so their FLUX 3 / Luma Uni-1 / Canva Code 2.0 items were DROPPED for lack of a verifiable published time. Dropped as off-topic/stale/covered: Rebelle 8.3 brushes-vs-AI (already covered 07-27..08-01), uxdesign 'Jakob's law one chat box' + 'Rethinking friction in an AI world' (both already covered), Google Earth Nano Banana rollback (covered), Snapchat AI-slop policy + Engadget lawsuits (no design workflow hook), 80.lv/roadtovr/uploadvr items (game-art/VR-hardware, not AI x design). Result: 6 fresh, design-relevant candidates across 3 distinct fetchable outlets (Creative Bloq, UX Collective, Figma) — enough for a diverse final 5 under the curator's <=2/outlet rule.

items.title: From Tinder and Reddit to Amazon, unwanted AI images are freaking people out
items.excerpt: Across Amazon, Tinder and Reddit, products are now silently generating or editing users' photos with AI by default, with opt-out left to the user. A pointed product-design and UX-consent lesson as generative image AI gets pushed into mainstream interfaces without asking.

items.title: Type designers have created a free font that 'poisons' AI
items.excerpt: ShieldFont is a free typeface engineered to corrupt AI training data that scrapes it, a craft-level countermeasure from the type-design community. Shows designers building AI-resistance directly into their assets rather than just opting out.

items.title: Creative technologists are moving from the margins to the center
items.excerpt: Once a fringe job title, creative technology is becoming a core capability inside modern product teams as AI collapses the gap between design and code. Argues the designer-who-builds is shifting from novelty to default operating model for AI-era design orgs.

items.title: Perplexity diverges with color: building data color schemes with generative AI
items.excerpt: A hands-on look at using generative AI (via Perplexity) to construct diverging data-visualization color schemes and palette tokens. A concrete workflow for folding AI into the systematic, accessibility-sensitive craft of color-system design.

items.title: A properties panel and annotations, now in Figma Make
items.excerpt: Figma Make adds a visual properties panel and annotations, letting designers edit AI-generated output directly and hand off intent to code without re-prompting. A real feature release tightening the design-to-code loop in Figma's AI builder.

items.title: AI fluency isn't the finish line
items.excerpt: Ninety percent of product builders call AI skills essential, but Figma argues teams are optimizing for the wrong ones and reframes what design craft means past basic tool fluency. A pointed take on how AI is reshaping the skills a design org actually needs.
